failures.evidence: THEY DO NOT: TestTheFanoutReportsItsOwnRefusalsForTheSessionsItDeliversTo (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/fanout_refusal_reports_test.go) PASSES against the pre-fix tree. I ran it outside the workspace, in a `git archive 196233c090e5` extraction with only that one test file copied in: ok 2.164s, all four subtests PASS, where at this head it is also ok 1.13s. A test that passes before and after the change it is offered as evidence for is not evidence. THE CAUSE is in its own table: its two portless rows set `SelfSubscribed: true` and take `core: true`, so the message reaches the fan-out through the core handler with no stored sequence; `delivery.Relayed` is then false whatever the entry says, and the branch the fix changes — `relayed && (verdict == takeFollowedTopic || target.Port > 0)` — is never reached. THE CASE THE FIX ACTUALLY CHANGES is a portless session on consumer delivery whose own consumer holds the STORED message, which needs a second recipient on the topic so the durable path reads it at all (takesStoredMessagesItself, durable.go:402, is true for any consumer-delivery session that holds the sequence). I wrote that test: TestAPortlessConsumerSessionIsReportedAnUnreadableDeliveryMode, commit 6d5c468e2eac on legion/INFRA-594-wip. At this head it passes; against the same pre-fix extraction it FAILS — `the exception lane of ses_portless_52241271… carried [], want one delivery_failed: nobody else reports a portless session's refusal`. So the fix is right and now has a lock; the round's own tests still need either replacing or keeping beside that one.

verifiedAtThisHead.what: The (session kind × verdict) matrix, walked against the code rather than against the comment
verifiedAtThisHead.observed: fanoutDelivery's branch is `relayed := err == nil && delivery.Relayed; if relayed && (verdict == takeFollowedTopic || target.Port > 0)`, and `delivery.Relayed` comes from Resolve's ConsumerRelaysStored, which is `ConsumerHoldsStored(storedSeq) && StreamCaptures(topic)`. So: a serving-port consumer session (Port > 0) is left to its relay for every verdict, and its relay judges and reports by the same rules; a portless consumer session is left to the fan-out for a refusal and to its relay only for a take, which is right because relayNATS publishes frames and judges nothing; a core-path session, portless or with a port, is never 'relayed' (storedSeq 0 or no consumer) and is reported by the fan-out as before; a session with no entry cannot be judged against a mode, so it is taken and its resolution fails, recording no attempt. The last of those is the one row of the implementer's own table I found no second way to read, and its test is the one subtest of theirs that distinguishes nothing either way.
